literal: Emperor Taizong did not follow this.
idiomatic: Taizong refused.

literal: Yue inwardly feared and doubted, hid a knife to enter attendance, and plotted great treason.
idiomatic: Fearful within, he entered court with a hidden knife and plotted treason.

literal: Shusun Jun suspected him, stole a look at his breast, saw a knife, seized him and ordered him to die.
idiomatic: Shusun Jun suspected him, glimpsed the knife at his breast, seized him, and had him put to death.

literal: His younger brother Chong—Emperor Shizu issued an edict ordering him to inherit Prince Huan's title.
idiomatic: His brother Chong was ordered by Emperor Shizu to inherit Prince Huan's title.

literal: Chong's nature was deep and steady.
idiomatic: Chong was grave and steady by nature.

literal: At first, after Prince Wei's death, Taizu wished to thicken clan kinship and ordered all princes' sons and younger brothers brought in to feast.
idiomatic: After Prince Wei's death Taizu wished to bind the clan and summoned princes' sons to feast.

literal: Prince of Changshan Su and more than thirty others all thought they would be implicated with Prince Wei; fearful, they all fled and were about to run to the Rouran—only Chong came alone.
idiomatic: Prince Su of Changshan and more than thirty others feared implication with Prince Wei and fled toward the Rouran—only Chong came.

literal: Taizu, seeing him, was greatly pleased, richly rewarded him with ritual gifts, and thereafter favored and honored him; Su and the others then were also at ease.
idiomatic: Taizu was greatly pleased, honored him richly, and Su and the others took heart.

literal: After long service he was appointed Regional Inspector of Bingzhou and had governing achievement.
idiomatic: In time he became inspector of Bingzhou and governed well.

literal: On campaign against the Rouran he separately directed the armies out through the Great Marsh, crossed Zhuoye Mountain, and awed the northern desert.
idiomatic: On campaign against the Rouran he led armies through the Great Marsh, crossed Zhuoye Mountain, and awed the northern desert.

literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Jing.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Prince Jing.

literal: His son Jian inherited; the title was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: His son Jian inherited; the rank was reduced to duke.

literal: He held the posts of General Who Guards the North and Great Commander of Huaihuang Garrison.
idiomatic: He served as general who guards the north and great commander of Huaihuang Garrison.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Jian's son Chen was Regional Inspector of Heng and Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Jian's son Chen was inspector of Heng and Shuozhou.

literal: Chen's son Yi was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Chen's son Yi was left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Qian's elder brother Yi was grave, spoke little, and Taizu often respected him.
idiomatic: Qian's elder brother Yi was grave and sparing of speech; Taizu respected him.

literal: He had fine strategy; following the pacification of Zhongshan he was granted the marquisate of Pucheng and made Administrator of Pinglu, received exceptional favor, was given drums, pipes, and feather banners, and treated with ritual equal to a great provincial lord.
idiomatic: Skilled in strategy, he followed the pacification of Zhongshan, was made Marquis of Pucheng and administrator of Pinglu, and received drums, pipes, and banners with honors equal to a great lord.

literal: In governing his post he was famed for authority and trust.
idiomatic: In office he was famed for authority and trust.

literal: After seven years in office Yuan Yigan was sent to replace Yi in the commandery.
idiomatic: After seven years Yuan Yigan was sent to replace him.

literal: At that time Yigan's son Wanyan had won Taizu's favor; Yigan relied on his son, slighted Yi, did not announce his arrival, and came with light cavalry that suddenly arrived, pushed Yi off the couch, and took Yi's seat.
idiomatic: Yigan's son Wanyan had Taizu's favor; Yigan slighted Yi, gave no notice, arrived with light cavalry, pushed Yi from the couch, and took his seat.

literal: Yi did not know he was being replaced and thought he was seized for a crime; once he knew, he was shamed by the insult and said to Yigan, "When my term is full and I am replaced—that is normal;
idiomatic: Yi thought himself arrested for crime; learning the truth, he was shamed and said to Yigan, "When my term ends and I am replaced—that is normal;

literal: your rude insult—how can it be borne!"
idiomatic: your rude insult—how can it be borne!"

literal: " He then grappled and killed him and reported the full circumstances.
idiomatic: He grappled with him and killed him, then reported all to the throne.

literal: Taizu admired this.
idiomatic: Taizu admired his act.

literal: Wanyan repeatedly appealed; an edict then ordered Yi to pay ransom.
idiomatic: Wanyan appealed repeatedly; an edict ordered Yi to pay ransom.

literal: Yi then asked punishment for himself; Taizu pardoned him and again waived the ransom.
idiomatic: Yi asked punishment for himself; Taizu pardoned him and waived the ransom.

literal: He died of illness.
idiomatic: He died of illness.

literal: Prince of Piling Shun was a son of Diggan, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: Shun, Prince of Piling, was son of Diggan, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: His nature was loose and obstinate.
idiomatic: He was loose and obstinate by nature.

literal: At the start of Dengguo he was granted the title Duke of Nan'an.
idiomatic: At the start of Dengguo he was made Duke of Nan'an.

literal: When Taizu campaigned against Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.
idiomatic: When Taizu marched on Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.

literal: After the defeat at Baixi, soldiers who had fled back said the great army had scattered in flight and no one knew where Taizu was.
idiomatic: After defeat at Baixi, fugitive soldiers said the main army had scattered and no one knew where Taizu was.

literal: Shun heard this and wished to set himself up; Mo Ti remonstrated and he stopped.
idiomatic: Shun heard and meant to declare himself ruler; Mo Ti dissuaded him.

literal: At that time Helijuan and others gathered a host and rebelled at Yin Guan; Shun attacked but could not overcome them, then left the palace, went south from Baideng into the old city of Fanchi, and blocked the Zhaishui as a defense to steady hearts.
idiomatic: Helijuan rebelled at Yin Guan; Shun failed to suppress him, left the palace, entered old Fanchi south from Baideng, and held the Zhaishui to steady hearts.

literal: Taizu approved this, advanced his enfeoffment to prince, and made him Colonel Director of Retainers.
idiomatic: Taizu approved, raised him to prince, and made him colonel director of retainers.

literal: Taizu loved Huang-Lao doctrine and often summoned princes and court ministers to expound it in person; those seated none failed to be reverent—Shun alone sat dozing, stretched, paid no heed, and spat.
idiomatic: Taizu loved Huang-Lao and lectured princes and ministers in person; all sat in reverence—Shun alone dozed, stretched, and spat.

literal: Taizu was angry and deposed him.
idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and deposed him.

literal: He died at home as a prince.
idiomatic: He died at home, still a prince.

literal: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie was a son of Lizhen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.
idiomatic: Yilie, Duke of Liaoxi, was son of Lizhen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: He had earlier been lost to Murong Chui; when Taizu campaigned on Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children and came to welcome him at Jingxing.
idiomatic: He had been lost to Murong Chui; when Taizu marched on Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children and welcomed him at Jingxing.

literal: When the central plains were pacified he had merit in battle and capture; he was granted Duke of Liaoxi and made Administrator of Guangping.
idiomatic: When the central plains were pacified he won merit in battle and was made Duke of Liaoxi and administrator of Guangping.

literal: At that time Heba was Mobile Court Commissioner at Ye; Yilie was bold and upright by nature, considered himself imperial kin, and was shamed to stand below Heba; he secretly gathered a faction and was about to raid Ye—discovered and ordered to die.
idiomatic: Heba held the mobile court at Ye; Yilie, bold and of imperial blood, was shamed to serve under him, plotted to seize Ye, was discovered, and was put to death.

literal: His son Bagan was broadly learned in past and present.
idiomatic: His son Bagan was learned in past and present.

literal: Though the father had guilt, Taizu, because Bagan was clan kin, entrusted him as a trusted intimate.
idiomatic: Though the father was guilty, Taizu trusted Bagan as kin.

literal: He had stratagems and repeatedly showed loyal diligence.
idiomatic: He had stratagems and served loyally again and again.

literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he was made Administrator of Bohai; officials and people were glad.
idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he became administrator of Bohai; officials and people rejoiced.

literal: He was granted the marquisate of Wusui.
idiomatic: He was made Marquis of Wusui.

literal: Transferred to Commander of Pingyuan Garrison, he won officers' and soldiers' hearts.
idiomatic: Transferred to commander of Pingyuan Garrison, he won the troops' hearts.

literal: He died; posthumous title Duke Ling.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Duke Ling.

literal: His son Shouluo inherited and was advanced to Duke of Wuyi.
idiomatic: His son Shouluo inherited and was advanced to Duke of Wuyi.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Chinu was Commander of Wuchuan Garrison.
idiomatic: His son Chinu commanded Wuchuan Garrison.

literal: Chinu's son Hongchao had considerable learning.
idiomatic: Chinu's son Hongchao was widely learned.

literal: After the Dacheng bandit turmoil an edict made Hongchao Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate to soothe and comfort Jizhou.
idiomatic: After the Dacheng rebellion Hongchao was sent with credentials as attendant at the Yellow Gate to soothe Jizhou.

literal: On return he submitted: "Jizhou's land is broad; its borders lie six or seven hundred li from the provincial seat; it backs on the sea, dangerous and remote—a separate province should be set to guard the coast."
idiomatic: On return he wrote: "Jizhou is vast; its borders lie six or seven hundred li from the seat; it backs on a dangerous coast—a separate province should guard the shore."

literal: " Court discussion followed this; later Cangzhou was established.
idiomatic: The court agreed; Cangzhou was later established.

literal: He died while Northern Army General [14] and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He died as northern army general [14] and grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: Yilie's younger brother Bo was skilled at archery and charioteering; for merit he was granted Duke of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Yilie's brother Bo was skilled at archery and driving; for merit he was made Duke of Pengcheng.

literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: His eldest son Su inherited.
idiomatic: His eldest son Su inherited.

literal: In Emperor Shizu's time he directed the armies stationed on the southern desert.
idiomatic: Under Shizu he directed armies stationed on the southern desert.

literal: The Rouran
idiomatic: The Rouran

literal: 〈lacuna〉
idiomatic: 〈lacuna〉

literal: memorialized the court.
idiomatic: and reported it in a memorial.

literal: Su was bright and upright, good at commanding the multitude; in comforting officers and soldiers he always shared their toil and rest.
idiomatic: Su was upright and skilled at command; he shared toil and rest with his men.

literal: On the campaign against Helong he was advanced to prince for merit.
idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he was raised to prince for merit.

literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Su's younger brother Hun from youth was skilled at bow and horse; Emperor Shizu praised him.
idiomatic: Su's brother Hun was skilled with bow and horse from youth; Shizu praised him.

literal: When envoys came from all quarters Hun shot three beasts—every arrow struck—and all seated thought it excellent.
idiomatic: When envoys from many regions came, Hun shot three beasts, every arrow true, and all at table admired him.

literal: When he became Master of Writing for Palace Affairs he was rather proud and unrestrained in fault; for an offense he was dismissed.
idiomatic: As master of writing for palace affairs he grew proud and unrestrained and was dismissed for an offense.

literal: He was moved to Changshe and was killed by someone.
idiomatic: He was sent to Changshe and murdered.

literal: Emperor Zhaocheng's son Kuduo.
idiomatic: Kuduo, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

literal: After Emperor Zhaocheng died, Fu Luo, because he was older, forced him to move to Chang'an; Fu Jian treated him with ritual and taught him letters and learning.
idiomatic: After Zhaocheng died, Fu Luo forced him to Chang'an for his seniority; Fu Jian honored him and taught him letters.

literal: In the turmoil he followed Murong Yong east and Yong made him Administrator of Xinxing.
idiomatic: In the turmoil he followed Murong Yong east; Yong made him administrator of Xinxing.

literal: After Liu Xian's defeat he sent his younger brothers Kangqi and others to welcome Kuduo; Kuduo then pressed the southern border and all tribes were stirred.
idiomatic: After Liu Xian's defeat his brothers Kangqi and others welcomed Kuduo; he pressed the southern border and tribes stirred.

literal: Taizu's attendants Yu Huan and others plotted to respond; a co-conspirator, Shan Wugan, reported it.
idiomatic: Taizu's attendant Yu Huan and others plotted to join him; Shan Wugan reported it.

literal: Taizu feared alarming hearts and hesitated without acting.
idiomatic: Taizu feared panic and hesitated.

literal: Three days later Huan told his uncle Mu Chong of the plot; Chong again reported it.
idiomatic: Three days later Huan told his uncle Mu Chong; Chong reported again.

literal: Taizu then executed Huan and five others; the seven surnames including Yu Mo Ti were all pardoned and not questioned.
idiomatic: Taizu executed Huan and five others; seven clans including Yu Mo Ti were pardoned.

literal: Taizu, fearing internal trouble, crossed north over the Yin Mountains, went in fortune to the Helan tribe, and sent An Tong and Changsun He to levy troops from Murong Chui.
idiomatic: Fearing civil strife, Taizu crossed the Yin Mountains north to the Helan, and sent An Tong and Changsun He to levy troops from Murong Chui.

literal: He fled to Kuduo; An Tong by hidden routes reached Zhongshan.
idiomatic: He fled to Kuduo; An Tong by hidden routes reached Zhongshan.

literal: Murong Chui sent his son Heluo with six thousand foot and horse to follow him.
idiomatic: Murong Chui sent his son Heluo with six thousand foot and horse to follow.

literal: An Tong returned with Chui's envoy Lan He, reached Niuchuan; Kuduo's nephew Yilie resisted.
idiomatic: An Tong returned with Chui's envoy Lan He to Niuchuan; Kuduo's nephew Yilie resisted.

literal: An Tong hid in a merchant's pack-saddle; at dusk he entered an empty well, escaped, and ran to Heluo.
idiomatic: An Tong hid in a merchant's pack; at dusk he entered an empty well, escaped, and fled to Heluo.

literal: The army had not yet arrived but the enemy pressed forward little by little.
idiomatic: The army had not arrived but the enemy pressed closer.

literal: Heranigan secretly harbored a separate design and came for Kuduo to invade the northern districts.
idiomatic: Heranigan secretly turned traitor and invaded the north for Kuduo.

literal: All were alarmed; none had a firm will.
idiomatic: All were terrified; none held firm.

literal: Then the northern great chief Shusun Puluo Jie and various Wuhuan fled to Wei Chen.
idiomatic: The northern great chief Shusun Puluo Jie and Wuhuan fled to Wei Chen.

literal: Heluo heard this and urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan, and others.
idiomatic: Heluo heard and urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan, and others.

literal: Once they knew Heluo's army was near, the host was somewhat steadied.
idiomatic: Once Heluo's army was known to be near, hearts steadied somewhat.

literal: Taizu went from Nushan in fortune to Niuchuan.
idiomatic: Taizu went from Nushan to Niuchuan.

literal: Kuduo advanced and encamped at Gaoliu.
idiomatic: Kuduo advanced and encamped at Gaoliu.

literal: Taizu again sent An Tong to Heluo and fixed a date to meet.
idiomatic: Taizu again sent An Tong to Heluo and fixed a rendezvous.

literal: An Tong returned; Taizu crossed Canhe, came out from north of Dai, and met Heluo at Gaoliu.
idiomatic: An Tong returned; Taizu crossed Canhe, came out from north of Dai, and met Heluo at Gaoliu.

literal: Kuduo, hard pressed, fled at sight of the banners and was then killed by Wei Chen; the emperor gathered all his followers.
idiomatic: Hard pressed, Kuduo fled at sight of the banners; Wei Chen killed him; the emperor gathered all his followers.

literal: Heluo took leave of the emperor and returned to Zhongshan.
idiomatic: Heluo took leave and returned to Zhongshan.

literal: Textual collation notes
idiomatic: Textual collation notes

literal: Book of Wei, juan 15: in all editions' tables of contents this scroll is marked "deficient"; the Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions have Song scholars' collation notes saying, "Wei Shou's book, the collective biography of Emperor Zhaocheng's descendants, is lost.
idiomatic: Book of Wei juan 15: every edition's table of contents marks this scroll deficient; Song collation notes in the Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions say Wei Shou's biography of Zhaocheng's descendants is lost.

literal: " The Palace edition's textual evidence says, "Wei Shou's book is lost; later persons supplemented it."
idiomatic: The Palace edition's textual evidence says Wei Shou's text is lost and later hands supplemented it.
